text.p: Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd on Thursday won shareholder approval to spend A$625 million on a share buy-back designed to ensure its independence.
Shareholders in Foster's, the leading Australian brewer and a major player in offshore beer markets, overwhelmingly approved the buy-back of shares from Japan's Asahi Breweries Ltd.
Asahi's stake, which represented 13 percent of the company, is being sold back to Foster's and cancelled as part of a major shake-out of the Australian brewer's share register.
Another major investor, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, last month sold down its 36.5 percent stake under an agreement with Foster's which ensured the shares were placed widely.
Foster's chairman John Ralph told Thursday's meeting of about 250 shareholders that the departure of both Asahi and BHP as major investors closed a troubled chapter on the company.
"BHP's support with that of Asahi during very trying times was critical to the survival and recovery of the company," he said.
Foster's, once debt laden and struggling to survive, said the way Asahi and BHP agreed to sell their stakes had ensured Foster's did not fall under the control of another brewer.
Together, they controlled 50.3 percent of Foster's.

"Shareholders have not only endorsed an important transaction for the company, but have expressed a vote of confidence in the future of a strong and independent Foster's Brewing Group," Ralph said after the meeting.
